stem: $O$ is the centre of a circle. {=t} straight lines are drawn across the circle. Exactly {=k} of them pass through $O$ and the other lines do not. How many of the {=t} lines are axes of symmetry of the circle?
solution: A straight line is an axis of symmetry of a circle only if it passes through the centre.
{=k} of the lines pass through $O$, so these are axes of symmetry.
The other {=t - k} lines do not pass through $O$, so they are not axes of symmetry.
